audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may count capital committed to the new plant as surplus cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for construction, start-up and ramp-up should be deducted from the $89.407 million bridge balance or charged as future OE investment supporting growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects the planned new composite materials manufacturing facility to be a significant capital project and, accordingly, anticipates funding-related expenditures from cash generated from operations, existing cash and marketable securities, and if appropriate, other available capital resources.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that the plant is a significant capital project expected to use existing cash and securities. Because the bridge supplies $89.407 million, or about 46% of the $194 million base equity value, an unmodeled commitment could materially change intrinsic value. The error amount is not demonstrated because no plant budget or forecast-capex schedule is supplied.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the approved plant budget, incentive package, construction and ramp-up schedule, and projected OE capital expenditures; rerun all scenarios with only residual excess cash added to equity.

audit_findings.title: The active ATM can make the cash numerator and share denominator describe different dates and claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.174 million gross proceeds and 869,852 shares; up to $1.23 per valuation diluted share before issuance costs
audit_findings.mechanism: The July share denominator reflects the June ATM issuance, while the May 31 cash bridge predates its proceeds, understating cash per fully diluted share.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company may, from time to time at its sole discretion, elect to sell additional shares of its common stock under the Distribution Agreement, subject to market conditions and other considerations.
audit_findings.explanation: The 10-Q demonstrates that the ATM was completed in June 2026 after the May 31 balance sheet through issuance of 869,852 shares for $27.174 million gross. The July 7 common-share count includes those shares, and the valuation uses an even larger fully diluted denominator. Adding gross proceeds would raise base value from $8.76 to at most about $9.99 per share before issuance costs, a roughly 14% change that is material to the valuation even though it would not close the gap to the $31.28 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June net proceeds and all option exercises or repurchases through September 6, then rebuild cash, liabilities and fully diluted shares at one common valuation-date cutoff.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be distributable at its gross bridge value
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.220 million deferred tax liability, equal to about $0.10 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A repatriation tax or transfer cost reduces the net cash bridge unless already represented as a future OE cash payment; the historical noncash tax charge should not substitute for deducting the liability and should not be counted twice.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded a deferred tax charge of $ 2,147 related to these undistributed earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies $32.7 million of foreign-owned cash and a $2.220 million deferred tax liability for undistributed earnings. Deducting the demonstrated liability would reduce the $194 million base equity value by about 1.1%, from $8.76 to approximately $8.66 per share, which is not material to the valuation conclusion. Additional withholding or transfer costs remain unquantified and are not demonstrated by the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the foreign cash, the $2.220 million liability and any withholding costs to the bridge, and verify that the eventual payment is deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The 2019 OE spike may violate the current-business perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.2 million FY2019 OE observation; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Discontinued-operation earnings, disposal gains or legacy tax items could distort the fitted OE trend and therefore the $7.4 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: However, mainly because of past operations of the Company’s former Electronics Business and operations of predecessor companies, which were generally in compliance with applicable laws at the time of the operations in question, the Company, like other companies engaged in similar businesses, is a party to claims by government agencies and third parties and has incurred remedial response and voluntary cleanup costs associated with environmental matters.
audit_findings.explanation: The former Electronics Business and the unusually high $30.2 million observation are established, but the supplied record does not establish that excluded-business earnings or disposal effects caused the spike. Depending on the trend specification, retaining an early high observation could raise the fitted level or steepen a declining trend and lower the current anchor. The valuation effect cannot be established without the contemporaneous OE bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2019 OE from the contemporaneous 10-K, classify continuing aerospace operations, divestiture proceeds, discontinued operations and legacy tax items, and rerun the identical anchor algorithm with any proven perimeter items removed.

audit_findings.title: Explicitly nonrecurring 2025 charges appear to remain in the anchor history
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.245 million of filed charges: $1.098 million storm charge plus $2.147 million deferred-tax charge
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalizing a one-time operating charge and noncash tax provision could increase historical OE and the fitted anchor, while the associated future tax cash payment belongs in the bridge or future OE exactly once.
audit_findings.evidence: As noted above, net earnings in 2025 included a $1.1 million charge related to storm damage incurred in May 2024 as well as a tax charge of $2.1 million for deferred taxes on undistributed foreign earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges are demonstrated, but the supplied valuation does not show whether its OE construction already removed their noncash or nonrecurring components. Their $3.245 million combined amount is 44% of the $7.4 million anchor, so treatment could matter. Under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule, the anchor cannot exceed latest OE of $9.8 million; reaching that ceiling would increase base operating PV by about $33.7 million, or $1.53 per diluted share, before separately recognizing the tax liability. Actual impact remains unresolved because the OE bridge and trend calculation are absent.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE bridge, normalize the storm charge with its tax and cash/noncash components, remove the deferred-tax accounting charge if noncash, deduct the related liability once, and rerun the unchanged anchor formula.

audit_findings.title: Environmental claims include an unquantified off-balance-sheet tail
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured remediation or legal costs would reduce future OE or require a contingent-liability deduction from the equity bridge ahead of common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company and certain of its subsidiaries have been named by the Environmental Protection Agency (the “EPA”) or a comparable state agency under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (the “Superfund Act”) or similar state law as potentially responsible parties in connection with alleged releases of hazardous substances at three sites.
audit_findings.explanation: Existing annual expenditures are small—$43,000 in FY2026—and were reimbursed or expected to be reimbursed, but that history does not bound the third site's exposure. The company is already a potentially responsible party, joint-and-several liability is possible, and no liability was accrued. The current claim is therefore an existing unquantified contingency, not merely a forward-looking monitoring item, but the record cannot establish whether it is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain site-by-site probable and reasonably possible loss ranges, allocation shares, existing accruals, insurance scope and limits, insurer credit status, and specifically quantify the uninsured third-site exposure before determining any bridge deduction.
